options: a:The driver only.,b:Only passengers on long trips.,c:All occupants of a car — seat belts are most effective when everyone is buckled.
note: Seat belts are most effective when every occupant is restrained; unbelted occupants become projectiles in a crash.

question: Why must you use extra caution near pedestrians carrying a white cane or using a guide dog?
options: a:They are blind, so you must yield and be prepared to stop to avoid injuring them.,b:They are deaf and may not hear you.,c:They are police officers.,d:They always yield to vehicles.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind pedestrian; you must slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop to protect them.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You never need to stop at a crossing unless a train is visible.,b:All crossings are equipped with lights and gates.,c:Not all crossings have flashing signals or gates; do not go around lowered gates and obey flaggers or signs.,d:It is legal to go around lowered gates during light traffic.
note: Some crossings lack active warning devices; always obey gates, lights, and flaggers, and never drive around lowered gates.

question: If you're taking a non-prescription medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the drug label for warnings about driving.,b:Assume it's safe because it's not prescribed.,c:Drink alcohol to counteract side effects.,d:Ignore any warnings and drive normally.
note: Many over-the-counter medications (including cold or allergy remedies) can impair driving. Read labels for warnings and ask a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the area faster.,b:Come to a complete stop every time.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a potential hazard; slow down and proceed with caution, yielding as necessary.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume and do?
options: a:Assume the driver may open a door and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes to avoid any sudden movements.
note: When passing parked vehicles, assume occupants may open doors or step out; slow down and pass with extra caution.

question: Which device is commonly used on highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement and signs.,b:White posts on the shoulder.,c:Flashing yellow lights.,d:Flashing red lights.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement and overhead lane signals indicate which lanes are for turning and which are for through traffic.

question: How should you prepare for potential hazards coming up on the road ahead?
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times so you don't miss anything.,b:Continuously scan the roadway and roadsides to identify hazards early.,c:Only watch directly in front of the vehicle.,d:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake to react faster.
note: Search and scan the entire roadway and its sides to spot hazards early and increase your ability to respond safely.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Only if an officer directs you to do so.,b:Only when police vehicles have activated lights.,c:Never; they must find their own path.,d:Whenever you see flashing lights or hear a siren
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using flashing lights or sirens by pulling over and stopping when safe.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is the driver's responsibility?
options: a:Do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and yield the right-of-way to them.,b:Always expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles.,c:Yield only to pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,d:Only yield if a crossing guard is present.
note: Drivers must be alert to pedestrians and yield the right-of-way to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Stop,c:Merge to the right and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn on multilane one-way streets or highways?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: When turning left from a multilane one-way street or highway, start from the leftmost lane and turn into the leftmost lane of the street you enter.

question: How can you help ensure your physical condition doesn't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Drive regardless of how you feel,b:Ignore doctor advice about driving,c:Know how medications affect driving
note: Be aware of medical conditions and medication side effects, maintain fitness, and drive only when it is safe to do so.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution across the tracks.,b:Rely on other motorists to warn you.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,d:Cross quickly before the train arrives.
note: If a train is close enough to pose danger, you cannot cross the tracks until it has passed and it is safe.

question: When may you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?
options: a:Whenever you turn on four-way flashers.,b:Only in an emergency; otherwise it is prohibited.,c:If you need to read a map.,d:If no part of your car is on the roadway.
note: Parking on the freeway shoulder is prohibited except for emergencies. Use hazard flashers and move fully off the travel lanes if possible.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:If the bus is stopped on the shoulder with no one aboard.,b:Only when students are crossing in front of the bus.,c:Never; buses must yield to traffic.,d:When the school's bus red lights are flashing and it is stopped.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights or its stop arm is extended.

question: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Cross quickly to beat the train.,b:Drive around any lowered gates if no train is visible.,c:Slow down and look both ways before crossing.,d:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail when signals indicate an approaching train.
note: If lights are flashing or gates are down, stop at a safe distance (at least 15 feet) and wait until it is clear.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:Temporary work zones or construction ahead.,b:Regulatory instructions like speed limits.,c:School zones.,d:Tourist information.
note: Orange signs typically warn drivers of highway work zones or construction and usually have black symbols or lettering.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When you feel like it is unsafe to cross.,b:Only if gates are down and red lights are flashing.,c:Only if a train is visible.,d:Only if directed by a flagger
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger or stop sign, and when warning signals, gates, or flashing red lights indicate an approaching train.

question: If another car is about to hit you, how should you warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Use your interior lights to signal them.,c:Speed up and drive away.,d:Sound your horn to alert the other driver or pedestrian.
note: Use your horn to warn others when you believe they may not see you and a collision may result.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you must pull over to the edge of the road and stop:
options: a:Regardless of the emergency vehicle's direction of travel.,b:Only if it is behind you.,c:Only if it is coming toward you from the opposite direction.,d:Only if the vehicle is identified as a police car.
note: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights and siren, regardless of whether it approaches from behind or ahead.

question: On a road with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:The side with the lightest traffic.,b:The same side as traffic is moving.,c:The side facing oncoming traffic (toward vehicles).,d:Anywhere convenient without regard to traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic when there are no sidewalks so they can see approaching vehicles and react if necessary.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, spirits) change how alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Beer impairs less than wine.,b:Hard ciders impair more than other drinks.,c:Wine impairs less than beer.,d:The effect depends on how much alcohol enters the bloodstream
note: The impairing effect of alcohol depends on the amount consumed and how quickly it enters the bloodstream, not the type of alcoholic drink.

question: May you drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Only if a flagger waves you through.,b:No — never go around or under a moving gate.,c:Yes if your vehicle won't damage the gate.,d:Yes if no train is visible.
note: You must not go around or under a lowered or moving gate; wait until gates are fully raised and lights are off.

question: Which kinds of drugs may impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only over-the-counter cold medicine.,c:Many kinds
note: Prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can all impair driving; check warnings and avoid driving if affected.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Start driving immediately because all cars function the same.,b:Only check the horn and headlights.,c:Hide any defects from the owner.,d:Familiarize yourself with the location and operation of signals
note: When driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to locate and test the turn signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector and horn; correct any safety defects before driving.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks that has no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and can stop on the tracks.,b:You can stop on the tracks briefly to check for trains.,c:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,d:You have enough room to get completely across the tracks without stopping and should never pass another vehicle as you approach the crossing.
note: Make sure there is room for your vehicle to clear the tracks before entering; never stop on the tracks or pass another vehicle while crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A flashing red light
note: A flashing red signal functions like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, then go when it is safe.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Keeping a larger than necessary following distance.,b:Always driving under the speed limit.,c:Driving too fast for conditions,d:Using turn signals too often.
note: Speeding, inattention, and tailgating are common causes of collisions; adjust speed and attention to conditions.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or vehicles,b:They are always more careful,c:They are fully aware of the risks
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time; even small amounts can affect driving ability.

question: By driving on Oregon roads, you have implicitly agreed to what regarding DUII testing?
options: a:You consent to take breath, blood, or urine tests if arrested for DUII.,b:You must maintain liability insurance forever.,c:You can refuse testing without consequence.,d:You're required to post bail immediately.
note: Under the Implied Consent Law, drivers consent to chemical testing when arrested for DUII; refusal has consequences.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Red.,d:Black.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; broken white lines may be crossed to change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You should merge immediately without yielding,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You must come to a complete stop before turning
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but requires yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: Stop lines painted across traffic lanes indicate:
options: a:Only where churches and schools are located.,b:The exact location where you must stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,c:An upcoming stop sign.,d:Where you may idle your vehicle.
note: Stop lines mark the point where drivers must stop at intersections or at pedestrian crosswalks when required.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.,b:Cross quickly without looking both ways.,c:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,d:Be prepared to yield to any train and cross only when safe.
note: Always look and listen for trains at crossings that lack active warnings, and ensure there's room on the far side before you cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do regarding other road users?
options: a:Sound your horn first.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk before completing the turn.

question: Which of the following affect how alcohol affects you?
options: a:Only the amount of food in your stomach.,b:All of the above (amount of food,c:Only your body weight.,d:Only how much time passes between drinks.
note: Blood alcohol concentration is influenced by how much you drink, the time between drinks, body weight, and how much you've eaten; food slows absorption but doesn't prevent impairment.

question: When changing lanes, what steps must you take?
options: a:Change lanes quickly without signaling to minimize time exposed.,b:Only check your blind spot after moving over.,c:Flash your headlights as your only signal.,d:Signal your intention
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: When is it permissible to cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:At any time,b:To pass traffic moving in the same direction,c:Only to make a left turn into or out of a private driveway or to enter/exit the roadway
note: A solid yellow line separates opposite directions of traffic and may be crossed only for permitted turns or to enter/exit the roadway, not for passing.

question: When are you allowed to cross double solid yellow centerlines?
options: a:To turn into a driveway.,b:To pass a slow-moving truck.,c:To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines prohibit passing or changing lanes; you may only cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, private road or to make a legal U-turn where permitted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate.,b:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way (the vehicle on the left must yield).
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right; proceed in arrival order otherwise.

question: When backing your vehicle, how should you look to check behind you?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window; do not rely only on mirrors.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Open the door to look behind you.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window; mirrors and sensors help but shouldn't be your only check.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are usually unimportant,b:They are only used in construction zones,c:They provide important information that helps drivers position vehicles and follow traffic rules
note: Pavement markings show lanes, passing zones, turn lanes, and other important guidance for safe driving.

question: When approaching any railroad crossing, what actions should you take?
options: a:Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop; if lights flash or gates are down, stop 15–50 feet before the tracks.,b:Increase speed to clear the crossing quickly.,c:Drive around a lowered gate if you are running late.,d:Stop only if you hear a train.
note: Slow down and be ready to stop when approaching crossings. If warning lights flash or gates are down, stop well back (15–50 feet) and never go around lowered gates.

question: What do pennant-shaped road signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Hospital nearby.,c:Speed limits.,d:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs (sideways triangular) indicate no passing zones.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Square.,c:Circle.,d:Octagon.
note: A stop sign is eight-sided—an octagon—and tells drivers to come to a complete stop before proceeding.

question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?
options: a:Across your neck for better support.,b:Hidden beneath the seat for comfort.,c:Snug across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belt comfortable across chest.,d:Loose so you can move easily.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hip bones and shoulder belts across the chest for proper protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best?
options: a:Proceed slowly and wait for an opening.,b:Turn on your hazard lights until safely merged.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and look both ways.,d:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach the flow speed of traffic and merge smoothly; traffic on the freeway has the right-of-way.

question: What should you do first when visibility decreases?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on interior lights.,d:Turn on headlights high beams.
note: Slowing down is the primary response to reduced visibility so you have more time to react to hazards.

question: When driving in fog, which of the following precautions should you take?
options: a:Maintain highway speed because visibility will improve soon.,b:Turn off headlights to reduce glare.,c:Use high beams to see further ahead.,d:Drive cautiously at reduced speeds
note: Fog reduces visibility; use low beams or fog lights, slow down, and avoid high beams which worsen glare.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:School zone.,b:No passing zone.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing; you must yield to trains and never try to outdrive an approaching train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way,b:Accelerate to beat the red light,c:Slow to a stop unless you are already in the intersection
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon turn red. Stop safely if you can do so; if already in the intersection, clear it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway from an on-ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the speed of traffic.,b:Enter slowly; freeway traffic will yield to you.,c:Stop at the ramp and wait for a large gap.,d:Drive on the shoulder until a gap appears.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, signal, and yield to traffic already on the freeway when merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You should force the other vehicle to stop.,b:Right-of-way alternates randomly.,c:You should speed up to get through first.,d:The vehicle on your right has the right-of-way
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather, when exiting an expressway, or when following motorcycles or bicycles.,b:Only when following cars that are smaller than yours.,c:You should keep the same following distance at all times.,d:Only at night.
note: Increase following distance in situations that reduce visibility or traction, such as behind large vehicles, bad weather, or when following motorcycles or bicycles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, which do you follow?
options: a:Honk to get the officer's attention.,b:Follow the officer's directions rather than the signal lights.,c:Wait for another officer to confirm.,d:Always follow the traffic signal regardless of the officer.
note: An officer directing traffic overrides traffic signals and signs; follow the officer's instructions.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Ignore the guard during busy hours.,b:Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the guard.,c:Assume the guard has no authority to direct traffic.,d:Follow the crossing guard's directions and use extra caution.
note: Obey directions given by a crossing guard in a school zone and be prepared to reduce speed and exercise caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: a:No one; you have the right-of-way entering.,b:Pedestrians,c:Only motor vehicles in the roundabout.,d:Only pedestrians in the roundabout.
note: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the approach and to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.

question: Under Oregon's Implied Consent Law, what have you agreed to by driving in the state?
options: a:To submit to a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for DUII.,b:To always carry proof of insurance.,c:To appear in court for all traffic stops.,d:To never refuse any traffic officer's request.
note: By driving in Oregon you consent to chemical testing (breath, blood, or urine) if arrested for driving under the influence of intoxicants (DUII).

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medication?
options: a:The medication will negate the alcohol.,b:The combination may multiply the impairing effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.,c:The alcohol will help the medicine work faster.
note: Mixing alcohol with medicines can increase the impairing effects of both and unexpectedly increase your level of impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes means:
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Passing is allowed only between dawn and dusk.,d:Drivers may not pass under any circumstances.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline indicates passing is allowed for vehicles in either direction when it is safe.

question: What is the single most effective thing to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Drive only on weekdays.,c:Always stay in the right lane.,d:Keep windows open.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce your risk of death or serious injury in crashes.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It only increases pollution,b:It can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment and cause poisoning,c:It can cause loss of hearing
note: A leaking exhaust can let deadly carbon monoxide into the vehicle interior; repair exhaust leaks promptly.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady yellow arrow, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow and stop if it is safe to do so, because a red arrow is coming.,b:Merge into the lane in the arrow direction.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the signal is about to turn red; stop unless you are already in the intersection and cannot safely stop.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:Half the width of a lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:The bicycle lane only.,d:To be followed more closely than other vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same rights to a full lane as any other vehicle; pass them only when you can fully change lanes.

question: What are the colors of signs that indicate distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Black with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Green with white letters.,d:Red with white letters.
note: Destination and distance signs on highways are green with white lettering.

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Lie down in your car and go to sleep,b:Walk onto the highway to flag down cars.,c:Stay with your vehicle and wait for help; you are more likely to be found if you remain with it.,d:Leave the vehicle immediately to walk for help.
note: If stranded in severe weather, stay with your vehicle, conserve resources, and wait for help; leaving may put you at greater risk.

question: May you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing when the train has passed?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances—never go around lowered gates.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing but the gate is still down.
note: Never go around a lowered railroad crossing gate; stop and wait until the gates are raised, signals have stopped, and it is safe to cross.

question: Signaling before turns or lane changes is:
options: a:Only needed during the maneuver,b:Only necessary if other traffic is present.,c:A required practice and a good driving habit — signal well in advance.,d:Optional in residential areas.
note: You must signal for at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; it is required and safe.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and then proceed when it is safe, just like a stop sign.,b:Slow down but you do not need to stop.,c:Yield only if other vehicles are present.,d:Ignore it and proceed normally.
note: A flashing red signal carries the same requirement as a stop sign: stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.

question: Your blind spot refers to which area?
options: a:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:The area you see in your rearview mirror.,d:The space directly in front of your bumper.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and slightly behind your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors without turning your head.

question: What is the most common color of general warning signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Blue.,d:Red.
note: Most general warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in line at a stop sign and the cross-traffic clears after the cars ahead proceed, what must you do?
options: a:Slowly roll past the stop sign without stopping.,b:Proceed without stopping since the way is clear.,c:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.
note: You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign each time and yield before proceeding; do not skip the stop even if traffic ahead has cleared.

question: Which of the following helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Using cruise control at high speeds in wet weather.,b:Driving with parking lights only.,c:Accelerating through puddles.,d:Keeping tires with good tread and proper inflation and reducing speed in wet conditions.
note: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning, ensure tires have good tread, are properly inflated, and slow down when roads are wet.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is true?
options: a:If weather changes suddenly, you should adjust your driving; slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you (All of the above),b:Weather changes rarely affect driving,c:Increase speed in fog for better visibility
note: Adverse weather requires slower speeds, greater following distance, and extra caution for other drivers who may not have adjusted.

question: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Take the right-of-way because you are in a vehicle.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Honk to get their attention.,d:Slow down
note: When encountering a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to avoid injuring them.

question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what occurs?
options: a:Your reactions slow and you make more errors while feeling more confident.,b:You become less confident and more cautious.,c:Your body metabolizes alcohol more quickly.
note: Increasing blood alcohol slows reactions, increases confidence incorrectly, and leads to poor decision-making and more driving errors.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution through an intersection?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop; right turn on red is allowed unless prohibited by sign.,b:Drive through if no other vehicles are present.,c:Proceed slowly because the light will change soon.,d:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light requires a full stop; turning right on red is permitted unless a sign prohibits it and you must yield as required.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact and avoid gestures.,b:React with hand gestures to show displeasure.,c:Distance yourself from the situation by slowing down or moving over safely.,d:Confront them to resolve the conflict.
note: When confronted with aggressive drivers, avoid eye contact and provocative gestures, and put physical distance between you and the aggressive driver.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver who is tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to scare them off.,b:Stop abruptly to punish them.,c:Speed up to create distance instantly.,d:Gradually slow down or change lanes to encourage them to pass.
note: If another vehicle is following too closely, slow down gradually or change lanes so the tailgater can pass; sudden braking is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat position so you can see and reach controls.,b:Your rearview mirror before adjusting the seat.,c:Your seat belt only, then drive.,d:The steering wheel before setting the seat.
note: First adjust your seat to a comfortable position with good visibility; then set mirrors and steering wheel as needed.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop then proceed when clear.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.
note: A red arrow means vehicles in the lane indicated must stop and remain stopped until a green signal or arrow appears, unless signs say otherwise.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels immediately to the left.,b:Back in without aligning first.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of the space,d:Turn your wheels immediately to the right.
note: Stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the parking space, signal, and then begin backing into the space.

question: A driver extending their left arm and hand downward is signaling that they plan to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Turn left.
note: A left arm extended downward is a hand signal indicating the driver intends to stop or slow down.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:Speed limit.,b:Railroad crossing.,c:Hospital ahead.,d:Stop.
note: The octagon shape is used exclusively for stop signs, requiring you to come to a complete stop.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Call the police immediately while continuing to engage with them.,b:Flash your lights and make rude gestures to let them know they're wrong.,c:Speed up and chase them down to confront them.,d:Stay calm and safely move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: If cut off by an aggressive driver, remain calm and get out of their way. Avoid escalating the situation by retaliating.

question: Why is it important to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations and avoid collisions.,c:It keeps traffic flowing faster.,d:It allows you to park more easily on the roadside.
note: Leaving space around your vehicle provides time and room to react to hazards or mistakes by other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The intersection is closed for repairs.,b:Make a U-turn because it is unsafe.,c:Proceed with caution through the intersection.,d:Stop and wait for the light to change.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution, watching for other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,d:Only commercial vehicles may pass.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean traffic in both directions is separated and vehicles may not cross to pass.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what actions should you take?
options: a:Drive away if damage seems minor,b:Only exchange insurance information and leave,c:Stop immediately
note: Stop, render aid if safe, report the crash when required, and wait for help; do not leave the scene of a reportable crash.

question: Your vehicle’s stopping distance increases under which condition?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways in good weather.,c:When driving at night only.,d:When traveling downhill always decreases stopping distance.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, or loose gravel surfaces, so reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: Which effects are caused by alcohol?
options: a:Improved reaction time,b:Loss of concentration,c:No effects at low amounts
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, vision, and concentration even at low levels; it is always risky to drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Turn the wheel immediately,b:Increase your speed,c:Signal in advance (about 3–4 seconds)
note: Use your turn signal several seconds before turning so other road users know your intent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed that is:
options: a:Above the maximum speed limit only.,b:Faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions,c:Exactly the speed of surrounding traffic.,d:Below the posted speed limit.
note: Drive at a speed safe for road, weather, traffic, and visibility. Legal limits are not always safe under all conditions.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as safely possible and stop until the vehicle passes.,b:Stop immediately in your lane wherever you are.,c:Proceed slowly and try to let it pass on the left.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: On two-lane roads you must pull as far to the right as possible and stop to allow emergency vehicles through.

question: When sharing the road with large trucks, what is important to remember?
options: a:Trucks always stop more quickly than cars.,b:They can always swerve to avoid you easily.,c:Trucks require longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles.,d:Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars.
note: Because of their mass, trucks need greater distance to stop; give them extra space.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than traffic all the time,b:Stopping only at stop signs,c:Weaving between lanes
note: Typical indicators of impairment include weaving, drifting, inconsistent speed, sudden braking, and delayed reactions.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windows and mirrors clear and allow extra following distance,b:Drive closer than usual to other vehicles,c:Reduce vigilance and rely on ABS
note: In wintry conditions, clear visibility and a larger cushion of space are essential because stopping distances increase.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you normally do?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder until you find a gap.,b:Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed and merge when safe.,c:Enter slowly and force other vehicles to yield.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.
note: Acceleration lanes allow you to increase speed to match traffic flow; yield to traffic and merge safely.

question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Ignore pedestrians since cars have priority.,b:Speed up and move into the right lane.,c:Stop in the middle of the intersection and wait.,d:Signal in advance
note: Signal 3–5 seconds before turning, slow gradually, move into the left lane as appropriate, and yield to traffic and pedestrians.

question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time between drinks.,b:Amount consumed.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage (beer,d:Body weight.
note: BAC depends on body weight, amount consumed, and time between drinks; the beverage type does not change the alcohol absorbed by the body.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Drive away if no one saw you.,b:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.,c:Leave a written note with your name,d:Only leave a note if the damage is severe.
note: If you cannot locate the owner after striking an unattended vehicle, you must leave a written notice with your contact information and circumstances of the accident.

question: What does flashing amber lights on a school bus indicate?
options: a:The bus is stalled and you should cautiously pass.,b:The bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children — prepare to stop.,c:The bus has finished loading and is leaving.
note: Flashing amber on a school bus warns it is about to stop; be prepared to stop. When red lights flash, you must stop.

question: What combination provides the best protection in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap belt,b:Only an airbag,c:A lap-and-shoulder safety belt used with an airbag
note: Belt and airbag together provide the most effective protection; airbags are supplemental and work best when belts are used.

question: What is a 'No zone' in relation to large vehicles?
options: a:A marked no-parking area.,b:The large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from view.,c:A one-way lane for heavy vehicles.,d:A place where passing is always illegal.
note: 'No zones' are large blind spots around big vehicles; avoid lingering in them to remain visible to the truck driver.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:The lanes move in the same direction and you may change lanes or pass when it is safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Passing is never allowed.,d:You must stop at the line.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes or pass.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Sharply away from the curb.,b:Slightly to the right.,c:Sharply toward the curb.
note: Facing uphill with a curb, turn the wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze first in cold or wet weather?
options: a:On exposed,b:In shaded areas such as sections covered by trees or buildings.,c:At intersections only.,d:On sharp curves only.
note: Sections of road shaded by trees or buildings tend to freeze more quickly and remain icy longer than other parts of the road; take extra care in shaded areas.

question: Drowsy drivers may:
options: a:Stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.,b:Drive so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated.,c:Drink coffee to become fully alert indefinitely.,d:Drive better on long straight roads.
note: Drowsiness can severely impair driving performance and may resemble the impairment caused by alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, what does it mean?
options: a:You may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection,b:You must stop completely before turning,c:You should merge into the lane indicated without yielding
note: A green arrow permits the movement in its direction, but you must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: If your vehicle begins to slide on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On slippery surfaces, first take your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle slows naturally; if additional slowing is needed, apply brakes gently and steadily.

question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes — it cancels the alcohol's effects.,b:Only if you drink a lot of coffee.,c:No — coffee does not lower your BAC.,d:Yes — it immediately decreases your BAC.
note: Caffeine may make you feel more alert but it does not reduce blood alcohol concentration or sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:The presence of a stop sign only.,c:How loudly you honk your horn.,d:Time of day only.
note: The gap you need to cross traffic safely depends on road surface, weather, and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, do not brake immediately, gradually slow down, and steer to a safe spot to stop.,b:Immediately slam on the brakes.,c:Immediately accelerate to stabilize the vehicle.,d:Turn off the ignition while moving.
note: On a blowout, ease off the accelerator, avoid sudden braking, slow gradually, and steer to a safe place to stop.

question: What is the act of looking over your shoulder to check a blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,b:A bad driving habit.,c:A good driving habit (checking your blind spot).,d:An unsafe maneuver.
note: Checking blind spots by turning your head is a correct driving practice and supplements mirror checks when changing lanes or merging.

question: How should you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights?
options: a:Pull over to the side and stop, yielding the right-of-way.,b:Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:See if you can reach your destination first.,d:Speed up and move away only if it is behind you.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping where safe; if in an intersection, clear it first then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What action is required at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,b:Stop only if other cars approach.,c:Stop completely,d:Ignore the light if you are in a hurry.
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and continue at the same speed.,d:Maintain the maximum posted speed.
note: When rain reduces visibility or road traction, slow down, turn on headlights and pull off if you cannot see clearly enough to drive safely.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the recommended procedure?
options: a:Reach down and try to pull the pedal up,b:Shift into park while moving,c:Shift to neutral
note: Keep control of the vehicle, shift to neutral, brake steadily, steer to a safe area, then turn off the ignition when stopped.

question: When must you stop for a pedestrian at an intersection?
options: a:Only if in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrian is directly in front of your car.,c:When the pedestrian is in either a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield and stop for pedestrians who are in marked or unmarked crosswalks; always give pedestrians the right-of-way.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do with your steering?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Turn your front wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, set the parking brake and turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection permit you to do?
options: a:Drive faster to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Always turn left without yielding.,c:Stop and wait for a pedestrian to wave you through.,d:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear and yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.
note: A steady green means you may go through the intersection if clear; turning is allowed unless a sign prohibits it, but you must yield as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a good general rule to remember about passing?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and legal.,c:Continuously pass slow vehicles to get to the front of traffic.,d:Always exceed the posted speed limit when passing.
note: Passing increases collision risk; drive with traffic flow, within legal limits, and only pass when necessary and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up suddenly to match the flow of traffic.,b:Pull off the right side of the road at a safe place and let the traffic pass.,c:Stop in the lane until traffic clears.,d:Maintain your slow speed and refuse to let others pass.
note: When you are impeding traffic by driving unusually slowly, you must pull off the road and allow others to pass where safe to do so.

question: Which of the following describes how alcohol affects you?
options: a:It slows reaction time, gives false confidence, and impairs thinking and judgment.,b:It improves coordination.,c:It enhances night vision.
note: Alcohol impairs inhibition, judgment, coordination, and reaction time; it can give a false sense of confidence while reducing driving ability.

question: What are dangers of worn or bald tires?
options: a:They increase stopping distance,b:They make turning more difficult,c:They raise the risk of hydroplaning (All of the above)
note: Tires with inadequate tread increase stopping distance, reduce traction, and make hydroplaning more likely; replace them when worn.

question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:Only when you see toll booths,b:On the main road just before the exit lane,c:After you have moved into the exit lane
note: Do not decelerate suddenly on the travel lanes; move into the exit lane and then slow down to ramp speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn you must usually do what to your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection.,b:Vary the speed unpredictably.,c:Reduce your speed to maintain control during the turn.,d:Keep accelerating until the turn is complete.
note: Slow to a speed that allows you to maintain control, stay in your lane, and react to hazards while turning.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck, what should you do first?
options: a:Blow your horn and signal other drivers,b:Slam on the brakes immediately,c:Shift into neutral
note: If the accelerator sticks, stay focused, shift to neutral, brake steadily, steer to a safe area, then turn off the engine carefully.

question: If you hear a siren behind you, what is the proper response?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are even in the travel lane.,b:Speed up to get out of the way quickly.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.,d:Turn into the opposite lane to create space.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind, safely pull to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

question: What should the driver of a small vehicle be prepared for when passing a large truck?
options: a:Reduced pollution behind the truck.,b:Wind gusts that can push a smaller vehicle off course.,c:Loud passenger announcements.,d:That the truck will slow to let you pass.
note: Large vehicles can create strong air gusts that may affect a small vehicle's steering; be prepared to correct steering when passing.

question: When roads are wet, what should drivers remember?
options: a:Roads are especially slippery just after rain begins,b:Give yourself more stopping distance than usual (All of the above),c:Hydroplaning is possible
note: Wet pavement can be especially slick early in a storm and increases the risk of hydroplaning; increase following distance and slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when driving in rural areas.,b:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,c:When someone is following too closely behind you.,d:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
note: Driving so slowly that you impede the normal flow of traffic can be illegal and hazardous; you may be required to pull over to let traffic pass.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Because traffic moves faster at night.,b:Because there are always more vehicles at night.,c:Because drivers cannot see as well in the dark and must use headlights between half an hour after sunset and half an hour before sunrise.,d:Because headlights are not allowed on highways.
note: Reduced visibility at night limits a driver's ability to see hazards; headlights are required during specified low-light periods.

question: When another vehicle approaches you at night from the opposite direction, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Use fog lights only.,d:Turn off headlights and use parking lights.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle at night; use low beams to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It improves driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It impairs both driving skills and judgment.,c:It only affects judgment at high doses.,d:It has no effect on driving skills or judgment.
note: Alcohol negatively affects vision, reaction time, coordination and judgment, increasing the risk of crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow centerline?
options: a:Never under any circumstances.,b:Only when turning left into a driveway.,c:Only during daylight hours.,d:When it is safe to pass or change lanes and you won't interfere with traffic.
note: A broken centerline permits passing or lane changing when safe and legal to do so.

question: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Keep going at the same speed in your lane.,b:Change lanes away from the stopped vehicle if possible; otherwise slow down and pass carefully.,c:Stop in the travel lane and wait.,d:Drive to the right and stop immediately even if on the freeway.
note: If an emergency vehicle is stopped with lights flashing, move over a lane if possible or slow down and give extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe,b:Slow and pass through without stopping,c:Wait for a flashing green light
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, yield, and go when it is safe.

question: What steps should you take when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal and change lanes immediately,b:Check mirrors and signal,c:Signal
note: Activate your signal, check rearview and side mirrors, glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear, then move over when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers behave when approaching an intersection with a steady green light?
options: a:Stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:Ignore pedestrians crossing the street.,c:Proceed if the intersection is clear but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection; be prepared to stop if the light changes.,d:Treat it like a four-way stop.
note: A steady green allows you to go if clear, but you must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection and be ready to stop if conditions change.

question: How should you drive through turns on slick roads?
options: a:Accelerate quickly while turning.,b:Change lanes quickly to maintain speed.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual to avoid skidding.,d:Brake hard mid-turn if you feel sliding.
note: Slow down before turns and drive through them more slowly than normal when roads are slippery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which has priority: a steady red light, a stop sign, or instructions from a traffic officer?
options: a:The steady red light.,b:The traffic officer's directions.,c:The stop sign.,d:All are equal; follow the most restrictive.
note: Directions given by authorized traffic officers take precedence over traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings.

question: An orange-colored sign most commonly means:
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction,c:A school zone is ahead.,d:A recreation area.
note: Orange signs are used to warn drivers of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations in or near the roadway.

question: Defensive driving is best described as:
options: a:Following the car in front of you very closely to block others.,b:Only driving when traffic is light.,c:Getting ahead of other drivers to reduce risk.,d:Identifying dangerous driving situations early and taking action to avoid accidents.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking proactive steps to prevent conflicts and collisions.

question: What are the typical colors of warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on white backgrounds.,b:Green on white backgrounds.,c:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background (work zones are orange).,d:White on blue backgrounds.
note: Warning signs generally use black symbols or lettering on a yellow background; work zone warning signs are orange with black markings.

question: A solid white edge line on the right that angles toward the center of the road indicates:
options: a:A parking area ahead.,b:You must turn left soon.,c:The road ahead becomes narrower.,d:An intersection ahead.
note: If the right edge line slants inward, it warns that the road will be narrower ahead so drivers should be prepared for reduced lane width.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what is required?
options: a:Slow down until it passes,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it then stop at the side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,b:Turn from your current lane after signaling at the last second.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.,d:Back up into the correct lane.
note: Do not make last-minute turns. Continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane to avoid dangerous maneuvers.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Ignore it if no lights are flashing.,b:Speed up to cross before the train arrives.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,d:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: Warning signs mean a train may be approaching; be ready to stop and obey gates and signals.

question: What is a good way to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Drive with one eye closed occasionally to rest the other.,b:Do arm exercises every hour instead of stopping.,c:Stop and rest every two hours or take a short nap if you become drowsy.,d:Drink energy drinks and keep driving.
note: Take regular breaks—about every two hours—and stop to rest or nap if you become drowsy to reduce crash risk from fatigue.

question: Which headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol?
options: a:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,b:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It lessens alcohol's effects on driving ability.
note: Mixing alcohol with drugs (prescription, OTC, or illegal) increases impairment and the risk of a crash.

question: You are in the left lane and want to move right. What checks should you make before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.,b:Check mirrors only and then move.,c:Signal and rely only on side mirrors.,d:Look over your left shoulder and move quickly.
note: When changing lanes to the right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder to check the blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes or passing?
options: a:Always use cruise control.,b:Honk and then change lanes immediately.,c:Stop on the shoulder first.,d:Signal
note: On interstates, always signal and check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes or passing; only stop on the shoulder for emergencies.

question: Signs that advise drivers of potentially hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Guide signs.,d:Informational signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions ahead; they are often yellow with black symbols or lettering.

question: On average, about how much alcohol does the body eliminate per hour?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,b:About one standard drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.,d:Half a drink per hour.
note: The average person metabolizes roughly one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service station.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and accelerate to the shoulder.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly,d:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: On a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, release the accelerator to slow gradually, then steer to a safe area off the roadway before stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You keep the same right-of-way to turn without yielding,b:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You may no longer turn and must go straight
note: When a green arrow becomes a solid green, the protected turn ends and you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: What should you know about large trucks when driving near them?
options: a:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,b:They need less room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,c:They have large blind spots and need more room to stop and maneuver.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and require more distance to stop and maneuver due to their size and weight.

question: While driving on major highways, what should you do to avoid 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Keep cruise control on at all times.,b:Close one eye occasionally.,c:Stare at a single point on the roadway.,d:Keep your eyes moving and stay alert to be ready for hazards.
note: Staying alert and moving your eyes prevents inattention and helps you react to hazards on long highway trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which vehicle may proceed first?
options: a:The vehicle that arrived last.,b:Only the vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle that arrived first.
note: At four-way stops, the first vehicle to arrive should proceed first. If two arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: Which of these helps prevent crashes by communicating with other road users?
options: a:Driving only on side streets to avoid traffic.,b:Speeding to get out of others' way.,c:Signaling your intentions and using your horn or emergency signals when appropriate.,d:Ignoring other drivers on the road.
note: Communicating—using turn signals, brake lights, horns, and emergency flashers—helps other road users anticipate your actions and reduces crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when entering public traffic from a driveway or private road?
options: a:The driver entering from the driveway or private road must yield to traffic already on the public road.,b:The public road traffic must always yield.,c:Neither must yield; proceed cautiously together.,d:Only yield if turning left.
note: Vehicles entering from driveways or private roads must yield to vehicles and pedestrians already on the public roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An arrow painted on the pavement within a traffic lane indicates:
options: a:Drivers in that lane must follow the movement indicated by the arrow (for example, turn only).,b:Drivers may choose to ignore the arrow if they are in a hurry.,c:Drivers must always come to a complete stop before following the arrow.,d:The lane is exclusive for buses only.
note: Pavement arrows indicate the required movements from that lane—drivers must follow the direction shown if they are in that lane.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right-of-way if they are in the crosswalk,b:Flash your headlights to hurry them,c:Speed up and pass in front of them
note: Always yield to pedestrians crossing in or entering a crosswalk; reduce speed and stop if necessary to allow them to cross safely.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition (All of the above),b:Only the driver's skill,c:Only the vehicle's color
note: Braking distance depends on speed, vehicle maintenance (brakes/tires), road surface, and visibility/conditions.

question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when merging onto a freeway.,b:When changing lanes,c:Only during night driving.,d:Only when other traffic is present.
note: Signals must be used for any lateral move or when pulling away from a curb; they are required by law.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Split the difference and squeeze between both hazards.,b:Pull onto the shoulder between them.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first,d:Pass the bicyclist first quickly and then deal with the oncoming car.
note: When faced with more than one hazard, avoid dealing with both simultaneously; let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist when safe.

question: A ''No stopping'' sign means you may stop only to what action?
options: a:Unload packages at any time,b:Diecharge passengers whenever needed,c:Avoid a conflict with other traffic (such as to prevent a crash)
note: A No Stopping sign prohibits stopping except to obey a traffic control device or officer, or to avoid conflict with other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you not do when changing lanes?
options: a:Use a turn signal to indicate your intentions.,b:Check for drivers who might also be moving into the same lane.,c:Fail to check side and rearview mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and blind spots and use your turn signal to warn others; do not rely solely on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you not pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the car ahead is signaling to turn right.,b:When a bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway.,c:On a hill or curve,d:When traveling below the speed limit.
note: Do not pass where your view is blocked (hill/curve), at intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, or other designated no-passing zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Stop before the sidewalk and proceed only when no vehicles or pedestrians are approaching.,b:Drive slowly to allow others time to get out of the way.,c:Honk your horn to warn pedestrians and drivers.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and approaching traffic, and cross the sidewalk only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your direction.,b:Slow down.,c:Pass with caution.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates passing is not permitted from your direction.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
options: a:0.10 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent.,d:0.05 percent.
note: Drivers age 21 or older are legally impaired and subject to penalties when their BAC is 0.08% or higher.

question: If you miss your exit on an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal to the driver beside you for directions,b:Get off at the next exit and return safely to the route you intended,c:Stop and make a U-turn at the median
note: Do not back up or attempt a U-turn on the highway; exit at the next ramp and re-enter the route safely.

question: If your wheels leave the pavement and drop onto the shoulder, what is the correct action to return safely?
options: a:Speed up and swerve back onto the road quickly.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,c:Reduce speed by gently braking,d:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: Remain under control, slow down gradually, then steer back onto the pavement at a safe speed; do not make sudden, sharp turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Treat it like a caution sign and continue through at the same speed.,b:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if not,c:Stop immediately even if it may cause a rear-end collision.,d:Accelerate to beat the red light.
note: A solid yellow means the signal is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop when traveling at 55 mph?
options: a:Less than a car's stopping distance.,b:Around 125 feet.,c:About 50 feet.,d:Up to 400 feet.
note: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars; a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph may require almost 400 feet to stop.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Maintain speed and keep steering as before.,b:Turn sharply onto the shoulder.,c:Hold the wheel,d:Brake hard immediately to stop quickly.
note: Keep control by steering straight, easing off the gas, and braking gently once stable; then pull off the road safely.

question: If your vehicle skids, what is the correct steering response?
options: a:Steer in the direction of the skid (turn into the skid).,b:Overcorrect the wheel to regain control.,c:Turn the wheel away from the direction of the skid.,d:Brake hard immediately.
note: If a skid occurs, stay calm and steer in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding to regain traction.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Reduce speed when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Drive faster to push water aside.,d:Turn sharply to avoid puddles.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, slow down in wet conditions, maintain tires properly, and avoid standing water where possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver in the largest vehicle.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right; that vehicle has the right-of-way.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over and stop immediately,b:Speed up to get out of its way,c:Continue driving normally
note: If the emergency vehicle is not displaying lights or siren, you do not need to yield; continue driving normally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The lane marked for bicycles.,b:The lane you feel like using at the moment.,c:The far-right lane always.,d:The lane closest to the lane you came from.
note: Turn into the lane nearest to your previous lane and avoid changing lanes during the turn.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that may affect safety, when should it be repaired?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible before driving.,b:Fix it only when convenient.,c:Drive at slower speeds indefinitely.,d:Ignore it if the vehicle still moves.
note: Any defect that affects safe operation should be repaired promptly and before driving whenever possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, what checks should you make?
options: a:Turn off your headlights.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Honk at least three times before passing.,d:Check mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal the lane change, and only return to your lane when it is safe to do so.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Brake hard and sharply steer back onto the road.,b:Stop your car on the edge of the road and re-enter when clear.,c:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.
note: If you run off the pavement, ease off the accelerator, slow down, check for traffic, and gently steer back onto the road when it's safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:At any time regardless of conditions.,c:When it is safe to change lanes or pass.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass when safe.

question: Which statement about work zones is true?
options: a:Work zones may be moving or stationary and require extra attention.,b:They are always marked with black and white signs.,c:You can drive normally and ignore them.,d:They only occur during daytime.
note: Work zones can be moving (e.g., mowing, striping) or stationary and are usually marked by orange signs. Slow down and be alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs tell drivers?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed for the road under ideal conditions,c:The speed to use in heavy traffic
note: Speed limits indicate the maximum (or minimum) lawful speed under ideal conditions; you must slow down when conditions require it.

question: Which is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.,b:You are less alert.,c:Your judgement of speed and distance becomes distorted.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts judgement about speed and distance; it does not improve reflexes.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light at an intersection indicate you should do?
options: a:Yield to other cars and continue at the same speed.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop because the red light is coming.,c:Go.
note: A steady yellow light warns that a red light will soon appear; slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.

question: What actions help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Before stopping,b:Release the gas and immediately slam the brakes.,c:Avoid sudden stops
note: To reduce rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops: release the gas to slow, then apply steady braking while signaling to following drivers.

question: How should you approach railroad tracks when driving?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop,b:Speed up to cross before a gate lowers,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate
note: Always look and listen for trains, obey signals, and never drive around lowered gates or ignore warning devices.

question: In a vertical traffic light arrangement, what is the top-to-bottom order of colors?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red,d:Red at the top
note: Vertically arranged traffic lights always have red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Try to get out of their way and avoid engaging with them.,b:Stare at them as they pass to show displeasure.,c:Speed up to challenge them.,d:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: Move out of the aggressive driver's path and avoid eye contact or confrontational behavior.

question: What can occur if alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:Nothing will happen,b:The effects of alcohol and the drug may both be increased,c:The effects may be reduced
note: Alcohol combined with other drugs can multiply impairing effects and produce unpredictable, dangerous reactions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop regardless of traffic.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Ignore it if no other cars are visible.
note: A yield sign means slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or roadway you are entering.

question: Hydroplaning usually occurs from what driving action?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet conditions, reducing tire contact with the road.,b:Frequent stopping.,c:Sudden turns.
note: Hydroplaning happens when tires can't clear water quickly enough at higher speeds, causing loss of traction and control.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Over your shoulder.,b:Straight at the oncoming lights.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: If oncoming drivers fail to dim their high beams, look to the right side of the road ahead to avoid being temporarily blinded.

question: What do work zone signs generally indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions ahead — slow down and use caution.,b:It is summer and roads are busier.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.,d:Roads are closed only at night.
note: Orange work zone signs warn of roadwork and changing conditions; reduce speed and follow directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean:
options: a:Only left turns are permitted across the lines.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is allowed at the top of hills only.,d:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean passing is prohibited from either direction; you may cross only to turn into a driveway or private road where permitted.

question: When must you yield to a stopped transit bus that is signaling to re-enter traffic?
options: a:Only if there are vehicles directly behind you.,b:Only if the bus turns on its hazard lights.,c:When the bus has its turn signal and activated flashing 'Yield' sign, you must allow it to re-enter by slowing or moving over.
note: If a bus signals to re-enter and displays a flashing yield sign, drivers must slow or change lanes to let the bus merge back into traffic safely.

question: When should you signal while preparing to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Early enough to alert other drivers of your intentions before you begin to pass.,b:Only as you start to change lanes.,c:After you have completed the pass.,d:Only if another car is beside you.
note: Signal well in advance of a lane change or pass so others have time to react to your intended maneuver.

question: Which device is most strongly associated with increased crash risk when used by a driver?
options: a:Radio,b:Cell phone (including hands-free),c:CD player,d:Map book
note: Cell phone use is a significant distraction and increases crash risk; any audio device can be distracting, but hands-on phone use is particularly hazardous.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:
options: a:Only at intersections with signals.,b:Only when pedestrians use marked crosswalks.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the street as the driver.,d:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic signals or crosses carelessly.
